questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x) &=(x^2-4)^2 \\ f'(x)&=2(x^2-4) \times 2x \\ &= 4x(x^2-4)=0\\ & x=0, \; x=2 \; \text{and} \; x=-2 \\ & \text{are the stationary points}\\ f''(x)&=4[x(2x)+(x^2-4) \times 1] \\ &= 4[2x^2+x^2-4]\\ &= 12x^2-16\\ f''(0)&=-16 \lt 0\; \text{ maxima at } x=0 \\ f'(2)&=(12)2^2-16 \\ &= 32 \gt 0\text{ minima at } x=2\\ f'(-2)&=12(-2)^2-16 \\ &= 32 \gt 0\text{ minima at } x=-2 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, there is only one maxima and only two minima for this function.

A single-phase half controlled converter shown in the figure feeding power to
highly inductive load. The converter is operating at a firing angle of 60[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]. If the firing pulses are suddenly removed, the steady state voltage ([latex]v_0[/latex]) waveform of the converter will become
questions.explanation: Single phase half controlled converter. As load is highly inductive, it means laod current is continuous and almost constant. [latex]\begin{aligned} &\text{During,}\\ &0 \lt \omega t \lt \alpha \\ &\text{freewheeling by }T_2D_1, V_0=0\\ &\alpha \lt \omega t \lt \pi \\ &T_1D_1 \text{ conducts }V_0=V_s\\ &\pi \lt \omega t \lt \pi+\alpha \\ &\text{freewheeling by }T_1D_2, V_0=0\\ &\pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 2\pi \\ &T_2D_2 \text{ conducts }V_0=-V_s\\ &T_1 \text{ is again triggered at }2 \pi+\alpha \end{aligned}[/latex] So, during [latex]2\pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 3\pi , T_1D_1[/latex] conducts. Now, if firing pulses are removed after [latex]T_1[/latex] is triggered at [latex]2 \pi+\alpha[/latex]. At [latex]\omega t=3 \pi+\alpha[/latex], no firing pulse will be available to trigger [latex]T_2[/latex]. So, load current will flow through [latex]T_1D_2[/latex] as load current is continuos. So during [latex]3 \pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 4 \pi,\;\; T_1D_2[/latex] will continue to conduct and  [latex]V_0=0[/latex]. At [latex]\omega t=4 \pi,\; D_1[/latex] will become forward biassed and [latex]D_2[/latex] will become reverse biased. So, [latex]D_1[/latex] will conduct and [latex]T_1[/latex] is already conducting. So, load current will flow through [latex]T_1D_1[/latex] and [latex]V_0=V_s[/latex].
questions.explanation_html:
Single phase half controlled converter.
As load is highly inductive, it means laod current is continuous and almost constant.

[latex]\begin{aligned} &\text{During,}\\ &0 \lt \omega t \lt \alpha \\ &\text{freewheeling by }T_2D_1, V_0=0\\ &\alpha \lt \omega t \lt \pi \\ &T_1D_1 \text{ conducts }V_0=V_s\\ &\pi \lt \omega t \lt \pi+\alpha \\ &\text{freewheeling by }T_1D_2, V_0=0\\ &\pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 2\pi \\ &T_2D_2 \text{ conducts }V_0=-V_s\\ &T_1 \text{ is again triggered at }2 \pi+\alpha \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, during [latex]2\pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 3\pi , T_1D_1[/latex] conducts.
Now, if firing pulses are removed after [latex]T_1[/latex] is triggered at [latex]2 \pi+\alpha[/latex].
At [latex]\omega t=3 \pi+\alpha[/latex], no firing pulse will be available to trigger [latex]T_2[/latex]. So, load current will flow through [latex]T_1D_2[/latex] as load current is continuos. So during [latex]3 \pi+\alpha \lt \omega t \lt 4 \pi,\;\; T_1D_2[/latex] will continue to conduct and [latex]V_0=0[/latex].
At [latex]\omega t=4 \pi,\; D_1[/latex] will become forward biassed and [latex]D_2[/latex] will become reverse biased. So, [latex]D_1[/latex] will conduct and [latex]T_1[/latex] is already conducting.
So, load current will flow through [latex]T_1D_1[/latex] and [latex]V_0=V_s[/latex].
